title: Building-brick toy set

fields.label: Page name
fields.help: Brand and set, e.g. Stackr Rocket Set.

fields.label: The set
fields.help: The set's name, the age it's for, how tall it is built, and three editions (colour versions) with prices. The page builds a brick rocket, so a space set fits best.

fields.label: Your bricks
fields.help: Optional: four numbers about your bricks (stud spacing, height, tolerance, testing) and what makes them grip.

fields.label: How should the page sound?
fields.help: A few words about the brand.

fields.label: Brand accent colour
fields.help: Optional: a bright colour for the main button.

writerNotes: The hero is a fixed WebGL animation: a brick rocket builds itself as you scroll (engine, fuselage and fins, nose cone) and launches. hero.title + hero.accent are the headline (the accent word is highlighted); hero.lede invites the reader to scroll and build the set by name. If the brand's set is not a rocket or vehicle, ask with _blocked whether the page may show a rocket.

sets.editions: exactly three colour versions of the set, each with a short name, a price (whole number), a card tint and the rocket's colours (body, accent, window, engine, tip), all picked from the brick palette: white, red, blue, yellow, dark, grey, orange, black, sky, green, pink, purple. The first edition is the rocket the hero builds. Leave out 'id'.

specs.items: exactly four numbers that count up (value as a plain number like 8.0, 0.005 or 1000000, a short unit, an optional prefix ±, and one line). They are claims about the bricks: use only the brief's numbers; if the brief gives none, keep the example's standard brick dimensions (stud pitch 8.0 mm, height 9.6 mm) and list the tolerance and testing paths in _assumed.
The tap-to-build baseplate, its palette and the brick diagram are fixed; builder.* is only its heading and instructions.

brand.name is the logo text and the giant footer word (letters wobble on hover); footer.fine is a one-line note (add a small-parts warning if the brief has one). theme.wordmarkFit: always "fit" for a new brand.
theme.accent is a bright colour for the main button and highlights (dark text sits on it): keep it light and saturated (yellow, orange, mint, pink).
business.name is set to exactly the name in the brief and cannot be changed.
